tools.name: check_message
tools.description: Paste any suspicious text — a message, email, marketplace listing, job offer, investment pitch or link — and get a plain verdict (REAL / SUSPICIOUS / LIKELY SCAM) with every check shown, a warning score, what to do next, a signed verdict certificate, and a shareable verdict link. Content is processe

tools.name: check_url
tools.description: Check one web link: it is followed safely server-side, tested for look-alike domains, domain age, sender rules, and the URLhaus known-bad list. Returns the same verdict, checks, certificate and share link as check_message.

tools.name: screen_urls
tools.description: URL defense: screen up to 25 links in one call. Each link is followed safely server-side and gets a verdict (REAL / SUSPICIOUS / LIKELY SCAM), a warning score, and its top warning flags. Private/internal links are refused per item and invalid entries are reported per item — one bad entry never fails

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "screen_urls" stacks urgency/override words (never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: URL defense: screen up to 25 links in one call. Each link is followed safely server-side and gets a verdict (REAL / SUSPICIOUS / LIKELY SCAM), a warning score, …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_message, check_url · Private data: screen_urls · Public sink: check_message, check_url.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_message, check_url · Private data: screen_urls · Public sink: check_message, check_url

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
